correctness.rationale: In each feasible nonconstant output run, the first and last centers are forced one site in from the bounding sites of the run. Differences between successive centers can only be 2 or 3 (independence and no coverage holes); zero-runs decouple the choices. Thus the local count is the composition coefficient c_(L−3), with infeasible lengths 1,2,4 and unique lengths 3,5,6,7. The all-one count is Perrin: cyclic steps 2 or 3 give (2z²+3z³)/(1−z²−z³) for positive lengths; n=1 excludes one by self-adjacency and n=2 gives two predecessors by the repeated-neighbor rule. For nonconstant indexed outputs, choosing the start label of a list of k run pairs counts each actual word k times even when periodic, giving the logarithmic derivative of 1−AB. Adding the separately counted constant outputs yields both stated series. Renewal weights include lengths 4 and 5, enforcing a positive simple unique dominant root by the triangle inequality and coprimality; its simple pole in the logarithmic derivative has coefficient prefactor one. Independent exhaustive finite check of every output and allowed input for n=1–16 and both series passed; /workspace/branches/470b5e86-15db-4e21-b741-0bf9df05b45b/independent_rule254_check.py and independent_rule254_check.txt. Bisection gives ratio 0.978994288608, but complex-root dominance is analytic. The supplied script was inspected, not executed.
